scope: 26 traditional-practice source-level partial external checks, with priority on herbal safety, neonatal oil studies and historical/contextual reviews.

checks.findings: Literature review of traditional and contemporary plant use during lactation and postpartum recovery, including pharmacology/toxicology and sociocultural data. Mechanistic claims about phytochemicals are hypotheses, not infant health trial outcomes. Sponsor and review selection methods unresolved.

checks.findings: Global literature survey ranks plants from prior surveys and reviews and investigates scientific literature for 20 frequently cited plants. Citation frequency and potential biological activity cannot establish lactation safety or clinical benefit. Author interpretation is not clinical guidance. Funding and overlap with TH2-038 pending.

checks.findings: Systematic review of 111 studies (39 randomized, 36 cohort, 18 case-control, 18 cross-sectional). Pooled adjusted observational estimates showed no significant associations for examined major outcomes; heterogeneous exposures, imprecision and observational confounding preclude general reassurance. Verify primary membership including retracted research and funding before using pooled estimates.

checks.findings: Linked Xiamen, mainland China live-birth data 2013–2018: 195,824 pregnancies, 3,024 herbal monotherapy. Adjusted RR for birth defects 1.25 (95% CI 0.69–2.29) versus unexposed. Live-birth selection, prescription versus ingestion, confounding and wide CI constrain causal inference. No broad safety claim; sponsor role unresolved.

checks.findings: OBSeRvE UK assessor-blinded pilot, 115 healthy term newborns randomized; about 80% retained. Oil groups showed greater hydration but less improvement in lipid lamellae than no-oil group; no clear TEWL, pH or skin score difference. Pilot not powered for clinical outcomes; funding and product supply unresolved. No universal oil recommendation.

checks.findings: Hospital RCT in Dhaka, infants born before 33 weeks. Aquaphor infection RR 0.60 (95% CI 0.35–1.03); no statistically clear difference for that comparison. Likely same parent trial as TH2-073; secondary PMID 24853544 reports 491 infants, denominators require reconciliation. Not home-care evidence; funding and harms unresolved.

checks.findings: Dhaka hospital preterm emollient trial mortality report, 497 infants; reported relative mortality reduction 26% with sunflower oil and 32% with Aquaphor. checks.findings: Nepal Sarlahi cluster trial, 340 communities, 16,327 versus 15,676 births. Neonatal mortality 31.8 versus 30.5 per 1,000, RR 0.95 (95% CI 0.84–1.08). No clear overall difference; active comparator (two oils), not versus no oil. PMC access CAPTCHA; indexed report. No home recommendation; funding and full harms pending.
